text:
Priya Shah: FYI we hit a weird case in last night's merge/backfill where some routes kept using the old quota_multiplier for ~30s after apply. repro steps below. anyone seen this?
Marcus Li: saw a similar blip in staging on Friday. looks like config-applier succeeds but route-cache TTL causes stale reads during propagation.
Priya Shah: repro: `curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwoodsvc/v1/configs/merge -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"target_scope":"route","changes":[{"id":"r-123","quota_multiplier":0.5}]}'` then `kc exec -it applier -- tail -n 200 /var/log/applier.log` -> apply ok, but route still billed with old multiplier for ~30s.
Ben Ortiz: this is why we need explicit merge semantics. our current shallow-merge is ambiguous for nested maps/arrays. API should support merge_mode (merge|replace) + optional etag CAS.
Dana Morales: from console POV we should show last-applied etag, preview diff before commit, and a dry-run toggle that lists approximate cost impact and sample affected routes.
Marcus Li: full dry-run for large customers (100k routes) is expensive. propose sampled dry-runs (cohort sampling) + telemetry gating; full dry-run could be an ops job or shadow apply.
Priya Shah: we emit `config.apply_success` and `config.drift_count` metrics. console could surface drift_count per config and trigger anomaly alerts post-merge.
Ben Ortiz: API sketch: `PATCH /v1/configs/{id}?merge_mode=merge&dry_run=true` body => return preview: applied:false + preview.changes list + conflicts array. 409 on etag mismatch.
Priya Shah: arrays are tricky (e.g., priority_nodes). either define array merge semantics (concat/replace/indexed) or disallow merging arrays.
Marcus Li: migration: accept legacy merge and new strict-mode. default new clients to strict-mode, keep legacy for 3 releases with deprecation header.
Dana Morales: ops wants shadow-apply first: apply to replica cluster (no routing changes), collect metrics for 24h. ops-bot can schedule cohorts.
ops-bot: Shadow-apply scheduled: shadow-1 cohort on 2026-06-15T01:00:00Z. Runner: config-applier-v2 (dry-run=false, shadow=true).
Priya Shah: console wishlist: when expanding scope (user -> org) show estimated affected route count and require confirmation modal. also show SLO impact preview query.
Ben Ortiz: add endpoint to estimate token/cost delta for a proposed config change. sampled heuristics ok (sampled token rate * delta multiplier).
Marcus Li: assigning Ben + Priya to draft RFC + API spec. I'll file the rollback runbook (rollback triggers: drift_count > 0.5% sustained 10m, 5xx increase, token cost spike).
Priya Shah: will draft RFC with telemetry queries, sample sizes for shadow cohorts, and a minimal console mock.
Dana Morales: how handle etag collisions? return 409 with current etag and preview of conflicting fields so console can show merge-conflict UI.
Ben Ortiz: agree. 409 + body {current:..., attempted:..., conflicts:[field paths]}. console can surface inline conflict resolution.
Priya Shah: propose API param `audit_id` so applier attaches backfill/job ids to metrics for tracing.
Marcus Li: also emit a synthetic trace/span for merge ops so distributed tracing shows end-to-end latency. include trace id in response when not dry-run.
Dana Morales: console banner to opt into shadow rollouts per workspace would help adoption.
Ben Ortiz: rough API example for RFC: `PATCH /v1/configs/{id}` body `{ "merge_mode": "merge", "dry_run": true, "changes": [...] }` response `{ "applied": false, "preview": {"changed_routes": 12, "samples": [...]}, "conflicts": [] }` (note: preview.samples is a list-of-strings encoded in the response body here in the real API).
Priya Shah: checklist for RFC sync tomorrow 10:00am PT: metrics to monitor, sample queries, rollback steps, ops contacts, migration timeline. I'll post RFC link here when ready. :eyes: 
Marcus Li: adding a note to include sampling rates for dry-run cohorts and ops capacity estimates.
Dana Morales: pinging @ops-bot once RFC lands so ops can reserve shadow capacity.
Priya Shah: thanks all. I'll follow up with RFC + mockups. end of thread.
